html:
The Kawésqar, also called the Alacaluf, are a canoe people of the channels and islands of western Patagonia in Chile, between the Gulf of Penas and the Strait of Magellan.

For thousands of years they moved by canoe through the cold, wet fjords, hunting sea lions and otters, gathering shellfish and keeping a fire burning in the boat. They are among the Patagonian shellfish and sea mammal hunters, with the Chono to the north and the Yagán to the south. The Selk'nam and Aónikenk hunted on land to the east.

Sealers, missions and disease devastated them in the 1800s. In 1881 a group of eleven was taken to Europe and shown in human zoos in Paris and Zurich; most died there. The few Kawésqar left settled at Puerto Edén, and their language now has very few speakers.
sum: The Kawésqar, also called the Alacaluf, are a canoe people of the channels and islands of western Patagonia in Chile, between the Gulf of Penas and the Strait of Magellan.
